samples.summary: Version skew: already-installed CLIs can no longer log in against an upgraded backend. The guard now hard-requires `nonce`, `code_challenge` and a consent click for `?mode=cli`, throwing `BadRequestException` instead of starting the login. Every published `wafflebase` CLI before this change sends only `?mode=cli&port=<port>` (see the old shape still recorded at docs/tasks/archive/2026/03/20260315-cli-oauth-login-todo.md:473), so those installs get a bare 400 with no upgrade hint on the wire. The in-repo CLI is updated, so no lane catches this; it is acknowledged in the guard's own docstring ("a CLI predating the parameters can no longer log in"), and it is worth confirming the release notes / a version-aware error message carry it, since the backend and the CLI ship independently.
samples.evidence: packages/cli/src/commands/login.ts:57 builds the new URL; the pre-change consumer shape is `<server>/auth/github?mode=cli&port=<port>` (docs/tasks/archive/2026/03/20260315-cli-oauth-login-todo.md:473), which now hits `throw new BadRequestException('Missing or invalid nonce')` in canActivate.

samples.summary: `baseCookieOptions()` now derives the *session* cookie's `Secure` flag from `GITHUB_CALLBACK_URL`, which changes behaviour for two out-of-diff consumers of that flag: `POST /auth/refresh` (`setAuthCookies`, auth.controller.ts:484/492) and `POST /auth/logout` (`clearAuthCookies`, :475), neither of which is exercised by the OAuth login this change is about. The sample `.env` still tells self-hosters to set `GITHUB_CALLBACK_URL=http://localhost:3000/auth/github/callback`, so an operator who copies the sample, terminates TLS at a proxy and runs `NODE_ENV=production` silently downgrades an existing, working session cookie from `Secure` to non-`Secure` on upgrade. The risk is documented at self-hosting.md:133-139 and mitigated by `COOKIE_SECURE` plus a one-shot warning, so this is a flag rather than a blocker — but the sample line itself is what an operator copies.
samples.evidence: packages/documentation/developers/self-hosting.md:42 hands out an `http://` callback URL; packages/backend/src/auth/auth.controller.ts:484 sets `wafflebase_session` with `secure: secureCookies(configService)` derived from that value.

samples.summary: `login-url.txt` (mode 0600, containing this login's nonce + PKCE challenge) is deleted only in the `finally` around `waitForCallback()`. The new spent-launch page explicitly instructs the user to "press Ctrl-C and run wafflebase login again", and the callback wait is now five minutes rather than thirty seconds — so the documented recovery path is exactly the one that skips the cleanup and leaves the file behind. Nothing else in the CLI removes it: `logout` (packages/cli/src/commands/logout.ts) and the config/session modules have no knowledge of the file, so it persists until the next successful login rewrites it. Impact is bounded (owner-only file, secrets expire in five minutes) but the cleanup contract is only honoured on the happy path.
samples.evidence: packages/cli/src/commands/login.ts:330 (SPENT_LAUNCH_PAGE) tells the user to Ctrl-C; the only `rmSync(urlFile)` sits in the `finally` of the callback wait, which a SIGINT bypasses. No other file references `login-url.txt`.
searchedFor: grep 'login-url' across the repo (only login.ts, its test, docs/design/cli.md and the task doc)

samples.summary: The user-facing CLI doc still documents `wafflebase login` as a plain browser flow. The operator-facing self-hosting doc records the new behaviour (a consent interstitial, a five-minute window, and `400 Command-line sign-in requires an https server` on a plain-http non-loopback deployment), but the page a CLI user reads does not, so someone whose `login` suddenly 400s has no pointer from the doc they are in. Nested/user docs are not covered by the top-level design-doc link check, so nothing flags this.
samples.evidence: packages/documentation/developers/cli.md:22 and :30 describe `wafflebase login` / `--server` with no mention of the https requirement documented at packages/documentation/developers/self-hosting.md:128-131.
searchedFor: grep 'Command-line sign-in requires' across the repo

finding.summary: `COOKIE_SECURE` now feeds `cliLoginAvailable`, an out-of-diff consumer of `secureCookies` whose question is "can this origin hold a cookie an attacker cannot plant?" — the override answers a different question and moves that gate in both directions
finding.evidence: packages/backend/src/auth/github-auth.guard.ts:216 `return secureCookies(configService) || loopbackCallback(configService);`, consumed at github-auth.guard.ts:514 to throw `BadRequestException('Command-line sign-in requires an https server')`. Before this delta that predicate was derived from the callback URL scheme only. Now: (a) an operator who sets `COOKIE_SECURE=false` on a genuinely https deployment (e.g. to work around a cookie problem) silently disables `wafflebase login` for every non-loopback deployment — the CLI gets a 400 that names https, on an https server, with no log; (b) `COOKIE_SECURE=true` on a real plain-http origin makes `cliLoginAvailable` return true, starting the CLI consent flow on cleartext where the `wafflebase_cli_confirm` cookie the gate rests on is plantable — the exact case the comment at lines 208-213 says is refused rather than started. The fix belongs on the new code: `cliLoginAvailable` should consult the derived origin scheme, not the operator's cookie-attribute override.

verdict.reason: The cited code exists verbatim (github-auth.guard.ts:215-217 and :518-522), but the described harm cannot occur, because the property `cliLoginAvailable` gates on is produced by the same overridden predicate. `loginCookieName` (github-auth.guard.ts:234-239) and `loginCookieOptions` (:246-253) both derive `__Host-`/`Secure` from `secureCookies`, and those are exactly what mint and read the `wafflebase_cli_confirm` cookie (:657, :661-662 issue; :622 match). So the invariant holds by construction: the gate opens only when the consent cookie really is `__Host-`-prefixed, or the origin is loopback. Direction (b) of the finding (COOKIE_SECURE=true on a real http origin) yields a `__Host-`/`Secure` cookie that a browser will neither store from nor accept planted over cleartext — the CLI flow becomes unusable, not bypassable — and the same operator assertion already governs the session cookie (auth.controller.ts:536). Direction (a) (COOKIE_SECURE=false on https) is the gate working as its own comment at :199-213 states: without `Secure` the consent cookie is not `__Host-` (:238) and therefore genuinely is plantable by a sibling subdomain, so refusing CLI login is correct; the reviewer's proposed fix (consult the derived origin scheme instead of the override) would actually open that bypass. The only real residue is that the 400 message and the docs (packages/backend/README.md:113-118, packages/documentation/developers/self-hosting.md:124-131) still describe CLI availability as derived from the callback scheme alone — a minor wording/doc inconsistency under this lens's scale, not a blocking blast-radius defect.

finding.summary: Logout's `clearCookie` now inherits `COOKIE_SECURE`, so `COOKIE_SECURE=true` on an origin actually served over http leaves the session cookie in the browser at sign-out
finding.evidence: packages/backend/src/auth/auth.controller.ts:474-476 clears `wafflebase_session`/`wafflebase_refresh` with `this.baseCookieOptions()`, whose `secure` is now `secureCookies()` and therefore operator-settable. A `Set-Cookie` carrying `Secure` sent from a plain-http origin is dropped by the browser, so the expiring cookie never lands and the previously-set session cookie survives logout. The pre-delta derivation could only produce `secure: true` on an origin that had declared itself https; the new override can produce it on an origin that is not. Same class as the `Secure`-on-http dead-login the PR describes, but on the revocation path rather than the login path, so it fails quietly instead of loudly.

verdict.reason: The cited lines exist (auth.controller.ts:473-477 clears both cookies with baseCookieOptions, whose `secure` is `secureCookies(configService)` at auth.controller.ts:534-538, now operator-overridable via COOKIE_SECURE at github-auth.guard.ts:80-89,158-171). However, the claimed impact — "the previously-set session cookie survives logout" — is not reachable, because the setter uses the identical options: setAuthCookies spreads the same `this.baseCookieOptions()` at auth.controller.ts:484-498, and a repo-wide grep for `res.cookie(`/`clearCookie(` shows auth.controller.ts:475-476/484/492 are the only sites touching `wafflebase_session`/`wafflebase_refresh` (the other hits, github-auth.guard.ts:661-690 and auth.controller.ts:370-372, are the login/state cookies). So for any fixed configuration the clear's `Secure` equals the set's `Secure`: with COOKIE_SECURE=true on a genuinely plain-http non-trustworthy origin the login Set-Cookie is itself dropped by the browser, so no session cookie was ever stored to survive — and that misconfiguration fails loudly at login, since the same flag drives loginCookieOptions/loginCookieName (github-auth.guard.ts:234-253). On http://localhost (a trustworthy origin) both the Secure set and the Secure clear are accepted, again symmetric. The only asymmetric window is an operator flipping COOKIE_SECURE mid-deployment while still serving plain http, which breaks all new logins at the same moment and is identical in class to editing GITHUB_CALLBACK_URL's scheme under the pre-delta derivation. The blast-radius premise — a consumer of the changed symbol left inconsistent — fails: the single consumer (clearAuthCookies) is symmetric with the single setter by construction.
